nodes.name: Co-N,P-HCS Two-Step Synthesis
nodes.procedure: A simple and continuous two-step strategy was used to synthesize Co-N,P-HCS where diammonium hydrogen phosphate (DAP) served as both phosphatization agent and nitrogen source on HCS support containing Co single atoms, resulting in formation of asymmetric Co-N₃P₁ coordination structure.
nodes.source_text: Figure 2a illustrates a simple and continuous two-step strategy to synthesize Co-N,P-HCS, in which the diammonium hydrogen phosphate (DAP) was applied as both the phosphatization agent and the nitrogen source.

unit_operations.name: Step 1
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: formation of Co single atoms on HCS

unit_operations.name: Step 2
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: diammonium hydrogen phosphate (DAP) applied as phosphatization agent and nitrogen source

nodes.description: ORR performance in seawater-based 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the catalytic ORR performance of Co-N,P-HCS was evaluated by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) measurements with a rotating speed of 1600 rpm in seawater-based 0.1 M KOH solution... E_onset = 0.97 V... E_1/2 = 0.89 V... Tafel slope of 38.5 mV dec⁻¹... C_dl value of 134.6 mF cm⁻²... kinetic current density of 55.81 mA cm⁻² at 0.85 V

nodes.description: OER performance in seawater-based 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The catalytic OER... activities of Co-N,P-HCS were then investigated in the seawater-based 1 M KOH solution... Co-N,P-HCS required the OER overpotential of only 320 mV to reach the current densities (j) of 10 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of 121.5 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: HER performance in seawater-based 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The excellent HER performance in seawater-based electrolytes were also captured for Co-N,P-HCS... displayed a lower HER overpotential of 164 mV for achieving a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² and a smaller Tafel slope (109.0 mV dec⁻¹)

nodes.description: Overall seawater splitting in seawater-based 1 M KOH (two-electrode)
nodes.source_text: two-electrode electrolysis devices... Co-N,P-HCS-based system showed a comparable potential (≈2.12 V) for achieving 200 mA cm⁻²... excellent stability for more than 500 h... Faradaic efficiencies... 98.5% for HER and 98.8% for OER

nodes.source_text: The overall seawater splitting performance... in practical conditions (seawater-based 6 M KOH). Figure 7b shows that the Co-N,P-HCS-based system required the potential of ≈1.92, 1.97, and 2.02 V to drive overall seawater splitting at a current density of 50, 100, and 200 mA cm⁻²... continuous operation for 1000 h

the S-ZABs using Co-N,P-HCS as the cathode showed a comparable open-circuit potential (OCP) of 1.45 V... high peak power density of 208.7 mW cm⁻²... higher specific capacity (736.5 mAh g⁻¹)... excellent round-trip efficiency of 55.0%... negligible round-trip efficiency fading (only 2.4%) was observed even after 750 h

nodes.source_text: the integrated system could achieve an ultrahigh H₂ production rate of 497 μmol h⁻¹ in seawater-based electrolytes

nodes.characterization_summary: No distinct peaks observed for Co-N-HCS or Co-N,P-HCS, while Co-HCS displays diffraction peak at 44° from crystalline Co nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The detailed structural features of the obtained catalysts were first investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD). The Co-HCS displayed a diffraction peak at 44° ascribed into the crystalline Co nanoparticles, whereas no distinct peaks were observed for either Co-N-HCS or Co-N,P-HCS (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: No distinct Co-based nanoparticles observed in Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS, unlike Co-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images also confirmed that no distinct Co-based nanoparticles... could be observed in Co-N-HCS (Figure S11a,b, Supporting Information) and Co-N,P-HCS (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: No distinct Co-based nanoparticles observed in Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) and high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images also confirmed that no distinct Co-based nanoparticles... could be observed in Co-N-HCS (Figure S11a,b, Supporting Information) and Co-N,P-HCS (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneously distributed Co elemental mapping confirms absence of Co-based particles in Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ring-like selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information) and homogeneously distributed Co elemental mapping images further supported the absence of Co-based particles in both Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Densely populated bright dots attributed to single Co atoms uniformly scattered on carbon substrate in both Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS, confirmed by Co L-edge EELS signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) images provided a closer examination... The densely populated bright dots, which are attributed to Co atoms due to the obvious Co L-edge signals captured in electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectra.

nodes.characterization_summary: Obvious Co L-edge signals confirm bright dots are Co single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The densely populated bright dots, which are attributed to Co atoms due to the obvious Co L-edge signals captured in electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectra in Figures S15 and S16 (Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-N,P-HCS shows Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 1248.8 m²/g and pore volume of 1.47 cm³/g with abundant micropores and mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms and pore size distribution (Figure S18, Supporting Information) verified that Co-N, P-HCS possessed abundant micropores and mesopores, accompanied by the high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface areas (1248.8 m² g⁻¹) and large pore volumes (1.47 cm³ g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-N,P-HCS shows higher I_D/I_G ratio than control catalysts, indicating abundant disordered carbon structure with numerous pore defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the D and G band peaks in Raman spectra revealed that the Co-N, P-HCS has a higher ratio of I_D/I_G than the control catalysts, implying its abundant disordered carbon structure with numerous pore defects (Figure S19, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES at Co K-edge shows position between Co foil and Co₃O₄; oxidation states determined as 2.01 for Co-N-HCS and 1.85 for Co-N,P-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) at Co K-edge... X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 3a) showed that the Co K-edge position of both Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS was located between those from the reference Co foil to Co₃O₄. Further analysis showed the Co atoms with an oxidation state of 2.01 for Co-N-HCS and 1.85 for Co-N,P-HCS (Figure S20, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows no Co-Co bonds; Co-N-HCS dominant Co-N peak at 1.45 Å (coordination number 4.2, symmetric Co-N₄); Co-N,P-HCS broad peak at ~1.65 Å from Co-N (1.45 Å) and Co-P (1.78 Å) bonds (Co-N₃P₁ structure confirmed).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform (FT) k³-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra are presented in Figure 3b... no peaks related to the Co-Co bond were observed... The dominant peak at 1.45 Å indexed to the Co-N bonds... the main broad peak located at approximately 1.65 Å might originate from the coexistence of Co-N (1.45 Å) and Co-P (1.78 Å) bonds... In Co-N-HCS, the average coordinated number of Co-N bonds was determined to be 4.2... each Co atom was coordinated with three N atoms and one P atom.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-N,P-HCS shows C, N, O, P, Co; N 1s: pyridinic N (398.2 eV), Co-Nx (399.3 eV), graphitic N (400.9 eV), oxidized N (402.4 eV); Co 2p: Co-N (780.4, 796.1 eV) and Co-P (775.9, 794.1 eV); P 2p: Co-P (130.5 eV), P-C (132.5 eV), P-N (133.5 eV), P-O (135.5 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S22 (Supporting Information), the XPS survey spectra suggest the co-existence of C, N, O, P, and Co in Co-N,P-HCS... The high-resolution N 1s spectra... can be deconvoluted into pyridinic N (398.2 eV), Co-Nx (399.3 eV), graphitic N (400.9 eV), and oxidized N (402.4 eV)... For the high-resolution Co 2p spectra... two new peaks ascribed to the Co-P bond appeared at approximately 775.9 and 794.1 eV... P 2p spectrum was divided into four peaks, which are assigned to the Co-P (130.5 eV), P-C (132.5 eV), P-N (133.5 eV), and P-O (135.5 eV) bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band maximum 6.98 eV for Co-N-HCS and 6.31 eV for Co-N,P-HCS; work function 5.33 eV for Co-N-HCS and 5.02 eV for Co-N,P-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3h and Figure S26 (Supporting Information), the valence band maximum (VBM) value was determined to be 6.98 eV for Co-N-HCS and 6.31 eV for Co-N,P-HCS... Moreover, Co-N,P-HCS had a smaller work function (φ = 5.02 eV) than Co-N-HCS (φ = 5.33 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ring-like SAED patterns support absence of Co-based particles in Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ring-like selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information) and homogeneously distributed Co elemental mapping images further supported the absence of Co-based particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneously distributed Co elemental mapping confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ring-like selected area electron diffraction (SAED, Figures S12 and S13, Supporting Information) and homogeneously distributed Co elemental mapping images further supported the absence of Co-based particles in both Co-N-HCS and Co-N,P-HCS (Figure 2d-h and Figure S11c-f, Supporting Information).
